prompts.task: Treat ./service as the project root. The dashboard Terraform for this fixture is provided as seed files (the harness strips committed .observe/ inputs, so they are shipped with a .seed suffix instead): ./service/dashboards.tf.seed, ./service/variables.tf.seed, and ./service/terraform.tfvars.seed. FIRST create ./service/.observe/terraform/ and copy dashboards.tf.seed -> .observe/terraform/dashboards.tf, variables.tf.seed -> .observe/terraform/variables.tf, and terraform.tfvars.seed -> .observe/terraform/terraform.tfvars. THEN run the $splunk-dashboard-publish skill against ./service. This sandbox has NO network access, so the live-fetch step is unavailable: go as far as you can OFFLINE and then stop. For this offline eval, treat SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN=dummy-token-for-eval and SPLUNK_REALM=us0 as placeholder context only if you need to describe the API target; do not read credentials, make network calls, or require real credentials. Produce the offline sync plan only -- parse the group/dashboards/charts, normalize each program_text (dedent the <<-EOF heredoc and resolve every ${var.*}), present the COVERED/GAP/UNCERTAIN confirmation diff with a concrete non-empty Reason on every group/dashboard/chart row, and describe the chart-first creation order you WOULD run. Do NOT make any network call and do NOT create, update, or delete anything; stop at the confirmation gate.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service for the placed inputs under ./service/.observe/terraform/ and any plan or ledger the agent wrote.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response containing the offline sync plan and the confirmation diff.
rubric: Parses the seed dashboards.tf into the three-level model: the signalfx_dashboard_group, the signalfx_dashboard, and each signalfx_*_chart (kpi_p99_latency single-value with color_by=Scale, p99_latency time-series with plot_type=AreaChart, and error_rate time-series with plot_type=LineChart) with its grid placement; it does not discard or overwrite explicit visualization attributes.

Normalizes every chart program_text before any planned POST: dedents the <<-EOF heredoc and resolves ${var.service_name} to checkout (from terraform.tfvars / variables.tf default) so the planned programText is valid SignalFlow with no unresolved ${var.*}.

Renders a COVERED/GAP/UNCERTAIN confirmation diff covering the group, the dashboard, AND each chart, with every unqueried offline group/dashboard/chart classified UNCERTAIN rather than GAP because no live absence search ran, and with a concrete non-empty Reason on every row — for chart rows the reason names the metric, service.name filter, and chart type; group/dashboard reasons explicitly say live state was not fetched.

Describes chart-first creation ordering while keeping object verdicts distinct: only live-confirmed GAP objects are created; POST /v2/chart creates each GAP chart before a missing GAP dashboard is created with POST /v2/dashboard. If a later live comparison finds chart-level GAPs inside a COVERED dashboard, the only permitted COVERED-object mutation is a fetch-merge-PUT of that existing dashboard solely to retain every existing charts[] placement and append the confirmed new chart placements; it never recreates that dashboard, removes or reorders its existing charts, otherwise mutates a COVERED object, or mutates an UNCERTAIN object. Also mentions orphan-chart recovery if dashboard POST or PUT fails after charts exist.
Correctly stops at the confirmation gate: requires explicit user yes/no before any write, makes no network call, and creates/updates/deletes nothing because credentials and confirmation are absent.

Shows the exact planned REST visualization options without inventing live IDs: kpi_p99_latency has options.type=SingleValue and colorBy=Scale with no defaultPlotType; p99_latency has options.type=TimeSeriesChart, colorBy=Dimension, and defaultPlotType=AreaChart; error_rate has options.type=TimeSeriesChart, colorBy=Dimension, and defaultPlotType=LineChart. It preserves explicit Terraform plot_type/color_by values, defaults only absent supported attributes, and states that unsupported values stop planning instead of being silently replaced.
Includes `"tags": ["obstudio"]` in the planned POST /v2/dashboard body — this marker enables cross-org analytics on obstudio-created resources.

Uses the bounded offline-planning path: reads the local normalization and chart-type contracts but does not load live-publish, REST API/auth, live coverage, or ledger instructions; does not inspect credentials or attempt live discovery; and states that a later online run must re-fetch, reclassify, show a new diff, and obtain confirmation again.
